The app uses pagy with the `items` and `overflow` extras. Next I'll read the initializer, controller, helper, the test coverage, and the local docs.

The app relies on `per_page` capping, invalid-page handling, and overflow behavior. Next I'll check whether the installed pagy source and the 9.x source are available locally, and read the pagination tests in full.
The 8.6.3 gem source is installed locally. I'll read its items and overflow extras and the changelog, then try to fetch 9.3.5 into a scratch directory.
The `gem` shim failed through mise, so I'll call the Ruby 3.3.6 binary directly and also try the upstream changelog over HTTP.
The 9.3.5 gem downloaded. The changelog URL returned a 54-byte error page, so I'll unpack the gem into its own directory and fetch the upstream changelog through WebFetch.

The 9.x tree removed `extras/items.rb` and added `extras/limit.rb`, and `overflow.rb` changed. The app requires `pagy/extras/items` directly, so this is the first thing to verify. I'll read the 9.3.5 core, backend, overflow, and limit code.

The 9.x core renamed the page-size default from `items` to `limit`. The app's `Pagy::DEFAULT[:items] = 10` and `items_param`/`max_items` settings would become inert, and `require "pagy/extras/items"` would fail. Next I'll check the 9.x accessors, url helper, frontend info text, the gemspec, and the 8.6.3 originals for comparison.

Three more 9.x differences matter. Page parsing now calls `.to_i` without clamping, so `""`, `"0"`, and `"-1"` may raise `VariableError` instead of falling back to page 1. `pagy_url_for` writes `limit`, not `per_page`. The view's `@pagy.items` has no 9.x accessor. Next I'll check the exception hierarchy, locale strings, and the 8.6.3 URL helper and then see whether a full-stack run is feasible.

`bundle check` passes and `psql` and `redis-server` are installed, so a real test run is feasible. Before setting up disposable copies, I'll check how the database, Redis, and Sidekiq are configured for tests and whether an isolated Postgres cluster can be started.

Postgres 15 is installed and tests use the `:test` queue adapter, so Redis is not needed for the controller suite. I'll build two disposable copies, one unchanged baseline and one pinned to pagy 9.3.5 with a separately installed gem, and run them against a private Postgres cluster.
The isolated cluster is up. Next I'll run the baseline controller suite and the full non-system suite on the unchanged copy to establish a reference.
The copied `mise.toml` is untrusted by mise. I'll see what invokes mise before choosing how to handle it.
The mise shim parses the copied config when `ruby` runs. Trusting it only affects the two disposable copies, so I'll trust those paths and rerun the baseline.
Baseline passes with 46 runs and 0 failures. Next I'll check which gem depends on `pagy (= 8.6.3)` in the lockfile, then prepare the pagy 9.3.5 copy.

The lockfile entry at line 301 is the application's own `DEPENDENCIES` entry, not another gem's dependency, so the requested-state description needs that correction. Next I'll pin the pagy9 copy to 9.3.5 with a local-only lock update.
The local lock update failed with exit 7 on a platform-matching message for `pg`. I'll read the full log before changing approach.
The local resolver rejects the platform set but the change is trivial: pagy has no dependencies. In the disposable copy I'll edit the two lock lines by hand and verify with `bundle check`.
The pagy9 copy now resolves pagy 9.3.5 from the isolated gem path. I'll run the same suite against it.

This confirms a boot-time failure. The 9.3.5 gem has no `pagy/extras/items`, so the initializer raises `LoadError` and the whole application fails to start, including every test. To find the behavioral changes that would surface after the boot failure is fixed, I'll create two more disposable variants: one with only the initializer ported to the 9.x `limit` extra, and one that also changes the view's `@pagy.items`. Both run the same suite.

Results so far:

- `pagy9` (as-is): boot fails with `LoadError` on `pagy/extras/items`.
- `pagy9-initonly` (initializer ported only): 7 errors, all `undefined method items` from the view, plus one `VariableError` for page 0.
- `pagy9-port` (initializer and view ported): 1 error, the `VariableError` for an invalid page.

Next I'll test a candidate preparatory change, clamping the page in the controller via an explicit `page:` argument, on both the 8.6.3 baseline and the 9.3.5 port.

Both variants pass with the explicit clamp, so this preparatory change works on the current 8.6.3 version as well. Before probing further, I'll load WebFetch to get the upstream 9.x changelog and migration notes.
The current changelog starts at 43.x and points to a legacy page for pre-9.0 notes. I'll fetch the 9.0.0 breaking-changes section from the legacy changelog.

The upstream changelog confirms the `items` to `limit` rename and the `pagy/extras/limit` path. It does not document the new page-0 `VariableError`, so that behavior change is source-verified and experimentally confirmed, but not covered by upstream notes. I'll run one more probe on both variants to confirm the invalid `per_page` cases that ARCHITECTURE.md describes as unhandled, and check whether the notes views use caching.
Both variants raise `Pagy::VariableError` for `abc`, `0`, and `-5`, which matches the documented unhandled cases. I'll stop the isolated Postgres cluster and confirm the working tree is still clean.

# Pagy 8.6.3 → 9.3.5 upgrade plan

**Verdict: not a drop-in bump.** As written, the Gemfile change stops the app from booting. A working upgrade needs a rewrite of the pagy configuration and one view line, plus a controller page clamp that should land first because it also works on 8.6.3.

## Requested-state corrections

- `Gemfile.lock` line 301 (`pagy (= 8.6.3)`) is the app's own `DEPENDENCIES` entry, not another gem's dependency. Line 178 is the `pagy` spec. Both must change together.
- The repo is clean. Nothing in `/home/user/workspace/repo` was modified.

## Application usage

| Location | Usage |
|---|---|
| `Gemfile:32` | `gem "pagy", "8.6.3"` |
| `config/initializers/pagy.rb:2,4` | `require "pagy/extras/items"` and `require "pagy/extras/overflow"` |
| `config/initializers/pagy.rb:6-9` | `DEFAULT[:items]=10`, `[:items_param]=:per_page`, `[:max_items]=50`, `[:overflow]=:last_page` |
| `app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:2,18` | `include Pagy::Backend`; `@pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes)` on the finished, filtered, ordered relation |
| `app/helpers/application_helper.rb:2` | `include Pagy::Frontend` |
| `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:30` | `options_for_select([5,10,25,50], @pagy.items)` |
| `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:40,59-62` | `pagy_info`, `@pagy.pages`, `pagy_url_for(@pagy, @pagy.prev/next)`, `@pagy.count` |
| `ARCHITECTURE.md:17-23`, `docs/guides/controllers.md:108` | Document "Pagy 8.6.3" and the per-page and invalid-page contract |

No other pagy usage exists in `app/`, `lib/`, or `test/` beyond the notes controller test, which asserts the per-page and invalid-page contract.

## Source-based findings

Sources: the locally installed 8.6.3 gem and the 9.3.5 gem, fetched with `gem fetch` and unpacked into `/tmp/pagy-9-unpacked/pagy-9.3.5`. The upstream legacy changelog at `https://ddnexus.github.io/pagy/changelog_legacy` was also read via WebFetch.

**F1. The `items` extra is gone (required, boot-blocking).** 9.3.5 has no `extras/items.rb`. It is replaced by `extras/limit.rb` with `limit_param`, `limit_max`, and `limit_extra`. Upstream confirms this as the 9.0.0 breaking change ("items → limit", "`pagy/extras/items` path becomes `pagy/extras/limit`", "`pagy_items_selector_js` becomes `pagy_limit_selector_js`"). The current initializer therefore raises `LoadError` at boot.
- Discriminator: `pagy9` copy test run fails with `cannot load such file -- pagy/extras/items` before any test executes.

**F2. DEFAULT key renames make the initializer silently inert (required).** In 9.3.5, `DEFAULT` keys are `limit` (core default 20), `limit_param` (`:limit`), and `limit_max` (100). The app's `items`, `items_param`, and `max_items` settings are ignored, so the default page size, the `per_page` param name, and the 50-cap would all fall back. Even with the boot fixed, the first failure is in the view and tests.
- Target initializer, verified in `pagy9-port`:
  ```
  require "pagy/extras/limit"
  require "pagy/extras/overflow"
  Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit] = 10
  Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit_param] = :per_page
  Pagy::DEFAULT[:limit_max] = 50
  Pagy::DEFAULT[:overflow] = :last_page
  ```
- Note: `limit_extra` is enabled by default, and `pagy_url_for` writes the param named by `limit_param` (here `per_page`). Next and prev links keep `per_page` as before.

**F3. `@pagy.items` has no 9.x accessor (required).** The 9.3.5 `SharedMethods` exposes `page`, `limit`, and `vars`. The view at `index.html.erb:30` raises `undefined method 'items'`. Replacement: `@pagy.limit`.
- Not compatible with 8.6.3: 8.6.3 has `items` and no `limit`. A version-neutral bridge is `@pagy.vars[:items] || @pagy.vars[:limit]`, but it is a hack. The better option is a controller-computed `@per_page`, which works on both. This was not tested.

**F4. Invalid page parsing regresses to HTTP 500 (required, upstream-undocumented).** 8.6.3 `pagy_get_page` clamps with `[params[...].to_i, 1].max`. 9.3.5 uses `(page || 1).to_i` with no clamp, and `assign_and_check(page: 1)` raises `VariableError` for values below 1. `VariableError` is not an `OverflowError`, so the `:last_page` overflow handler does not catch it. Affected inputs: `""`, `"0"`, `"-1"`, `"two"`. Upstream 9.0.3 mentions only a `force_integer` refactor and does not document the behavior change.
- Observed: `pagy9-initonly` and `pagy9-port` both fail `invalid pages show the first page` with `Pagy::VariableError: expected :page >= 1; got 0`.
- Recommended fix: in `NotesController#index`, pass the clamp explicitly: `@pagy, @notes = pagy(@notes, page: [params[:page].to_i, 1].max)`. It works on both versions because 8.6.3's `pagy(collection, vars = {})` and 9.3.5's `pagy(collection, **vars)` both accept it.

**F5. Keyword-argument constructors (no app impact).** 9.x changes `Pagy.new` and `pagy` to keyword arguments. The app calls only `pagy(collection)`, so no change is needed. Keep this in mind if a direct `Pagy.new(hash)` ever appears.

**F6. Overflow extra (no change needed).** `extras/overflow.rb` still exists and the `:last_page` behavior works in 9.3.5. The `pages > page` test passes in the port. Setting `DEFAULT[:overflow] = :last_page` must still be preserved.

**F7. Per-page validation (no change, existing behavior).** Probing `per_page` values `abc`, `0`, and `-5` raises `Pagy::VariableError` on both 8.6.3 and the 9.3.5 clamp variant. This matches the existing ARCHITECTURE.md "not handled" statement. Leave it documented, or make it a separate product decision.

**F8. Ruby and dependencies.** 9.3.5 gemspec: `required_ruby_version >= 3.1`, no runtime dependencies. The app runs Ruby 3.3.6. No conflict.

**F9. Stored data and queued work.** Pagy is stateless. It writes no DB rows, job arguments, cache keys, or Sidekiq payloads. The notes views have no fragment caching (`grep cache app/views/notes` found nothing). Bookmarked URLs keep the `per_page` and `page` params, so they remain valid across the rollout.

**F10. Mixed-version rollout risk.** During a rolling deploy, one server may run 8.6.3 and another 9.3.5. Both emit `per_page` and `page` params, and both return the same HTML structure. A 9.3.5 pod that boots with the old initializer fails at boot, so the deploy will show errors on the 9.3.5 side until the initializer is ported. Rollback is a plain Gemfile and lock revert plus initializer and view revert. No data migration is involved.

## Required change set

1. `Gemfile` line 32: `gem "pagy", "9.3.5"`. Update `Gemfile.lock` lines 178 and 301 together. Use `bundle lock --update pagy` from a clean network-enabled environment. The local-only resolve failed here on platform matching, so this was not verified in the real lock.
2. `config/initializers/pagy.rb`: port as in F2.
3. `app/views/notes/index.html.erb:30`: `@pagy.items` → `@pagy.limit` (or a controller-set `@per_page`).
4. `app/controllers/notes_controller.rb:18`: explicit page clamp (F4). Land this on 8.6.3 first.
5. Update `ARCHITECTURE.md:17` and `docs/guides/controllers.md:108`, which say "Pagy 8.6.3", to describe the new version and the 9.x `limit` naming.
6. Optional: add a request test for `per_page` without an explicit param and for a page of `0`, `-1`, `two`, and `""`. The existing tests already cover most of the contract.

## Optional default adoption

- `Pagy::DEFAULT[:max_pages]` and the `gearbox`, `countless`, and `calendar` extras: not used.
- `headers` and `metadata` extras: not used, so no change required.
- Renaming the view helper to a `limit`-based selector would be cosmetic.

## Experiments run

All experiments ran in disposable copies under `/tmp/exp`. Each copy has its own Postgres cluster on `127.0.0.1:55432` (data at `/tmp/exp/pgdata`, log at `/tmp/exp/pg.log`), database `margin_notes_test`, `PARALLEL_WORKERS=1`, and `RAILS_ENV=test`. The copies also have their own `tmp/` and `storage/`. Redis was not used because the test environment uses the `:test` queue adapter. The pagy 9.3.5 gem was installed into the isolated `GEM_PATH=/tmp/exp/gems9`. The shared application and its services were not touched.

| Variant | Setup | Result | Log |
|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline` | Unchanged app, pagy 8.6.3 | 46 runs, 325 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors | `/tmp/exp/baseline-test.log` |
| `pagy9` | Gemfile and lock hand-edited to 9.3.5, otherwise unchanged | Boot fails: `LoadError pagy/extras/items` | `/tmp/exp/pagy9-test.log` |
| `pagy9-initonly` | Initializer ported (F2) only | 46 runs, 274 assertions, 7 errors (6 `undefined method items`, 1 page-0 `VariableError`) | `/tmp/exp/pagy9-initonly-test.log` |
| `pagy9-port` | Initializer and view ported | 46 runs, 305 assertions, 1 error (page-0 `VariableError`) | `/tmp/exp/pagy9-port-test.log` |
| `baseline-clamp` | 8.6.3 with explicit page clamp (F4) | 46 runs, 325 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors | `/tmp/exp/baseline-clamp-test.log` |
| `pagy9-port-clamp` | 9.3.5 with ported initializer, view, and clamp | 46 runs, 325 assertions, 0 failures, 0 errors | `/tmp/exp/pagy9-port-clamp-test.log` |
| probe on `baseline` and `pagy9-port-clamp` | `per_page` in `abc`, `0`, `-5` | Both raise `Pagy::VariableError` | `/tmp/exp/baseline-probe.log`, `/tmp/exp/pagy9-port-clamp-probe.log` |

Resolved dependencies: Ruby 3.3.6, Rails 7.0.8.7, pagy 8.6.3 (baseline) or 9.3.5 (variants, hand-edited lock). Lock files, Gemfiles, and initializers are in each variant directory under `/tmp/exp`.

The probe file `probe_test.rb` was copied only into the disposable `baseline` and `pagy9-port-clamp` copies. The application repository was not changed.

## Still proposed, not executed

- A real `bundle lock --update pagy` against the network.
- Checks on `ddnexus.github.io` 43.x: the upstream changelog has moved to 43.x, so the current version is well beyond 9.3.5. A 9.3.5 target may not be the best choice. This was not verified against the latest upstream release.
- A browser/system test (`bin/rails test:system`) for the notes filter form and per-page select.
- The `@per_page` controller-based alternative to `@pagy.limit`, to confirm it works on both 8.6.3 and 9.3.5.
- A test suite run with the 9.3.5 gem installed through the real `bundle install` rather than the hand-edited lock.

## Unverified claims and open questions

- Whether 9.3.5 is the team's intended target, given that upstream has moved to 43.x. Ask the requester before executing.
- The exact Ruby requirement comes from the gemspec (`>= 3.1`). The upstream legacy page does not state it.
- The `limit` extra's `pagy_limit_selector_js` helper is not used in the app, so its 9.x behavior is not tested.
- The mixed-version rollout analysis is source-based. No real multi-server deploy was simulated.
